name: Nanophthalmos

criteria.description: Axial length of the eye less than 20 mm
High hypermetropic refractive error typically greater than +8 diopters
Increased scleral thickness observed on imaging
No other ocular malformations such as coloboma or microcornea
Normal corneal diameter differentiating from microphthalmos with microcornea

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: axial length <20 mm, high hyperopia, and thickened sclera
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by imaging and refractive measurements; genetic testing may assist in familial cases.

imaging: Ultrasound biomicroscopy showing reduced axial length and thickened sclera
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (OCT) demonstrating shallow anterior chamber
B-scan ultrasonography revealing thickened posterior sclera
genetic: Other genetic loci implicated in autosomal dominant and recessive inheritance patterns
other: Refractive error measurement confirming high hyperopia
Gonioscopy showing narrow or closed angles

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of other ocular malformations such as coloboma or microcornea
Normal anterior segment dimensions with short posterior segment
High hyperopia but normal corneal size
Less scleral thickening compared to nanophthalmos

redFlags: Sudden onset of eye pain and vision loss indicating acute angle-closure glaucoma
Progressive visual field loss suggestive of optic neuropathy
Signs of uveal effusion syndrome with serous retinal detachment
references: Huang et al., Nanophthalmos: Clinical and Genetic Perspectives, Survey of Ophthalmology, 2020
Orphanet Report on Nanophthalmos, Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases, 2019
MFRP Gene Mutations in Nanophthalmos, American Journal of Human Genetics, 2018
